description: Recovery catalogue for the seven-suite, 15,450-instance QACOBench release.

admitted_suites.name: ICWS 2007 Benchmark Scenarios
admitted_suites.rationale: Historical standard for QoS web service composition. Retains sequential task graphs, real-world candidate QoS matrices (response time, throughput, cost, availability, reliability), and linear multi-attribute utility scalarization.

admitted_suites.name: Quantum Service Selection Benchmark

source.title: Quantum Resource Selection as a QoS-Aware Composition Problem

admitted_suites.rationale: Exercises domain transfer of QACO to quantum circuit execution. QoS dimensions include gate fidelity, queue wait times, readout error rates, and quantum execution token costs.

admitted_suites.name: HSC-LLM (Hierarchical Service Composition for LLM Workflows)

source.title: HSC-LLM: Hierarchical Service Composition and Routing for Foundation Model Pipelines

admitted_suites.rationale: Evaluates multi-agent LLM pipeline routing across heterogeneous models (latency, monetary cost per token, reasoning accuracy, and rate-limit throughput constraints).

admitted_suites.name: RPRSR15 (Ramirez & Parejo Web Service Composition Benchmark)

source.title: An empirical study of GRASP heuristics for QoS-aware Web service composition / Optimization of service compositions with branches

admitted_suites.rationale: Lossless conversion of 60 literature instances from Ramirez et al. Features both sequential and exclusive branch (XOR) structures mapped to RoutingOverlay with branch probabilities, 5 QoS metrics, and non-linear utility aggregation.

admitted_suites.name: IoTS (IoT Service Composition Dataset)

source.title: An improved multi-objective optimization algorithm for IoT service composition

admitted_suites.rationale: Scalable real-world IoT service composition benchmark covering 10 to 60 tasks with candidate pools derived from 120 task workbooks. Features ResponseTime, Cost, Reliability, and Availability.

admitted_suites.name: BWS-SCP (Cloud Manufacturing Worker-Service Matching Benchmark)

source.title: Bi-objective worker-service matching in cloud manufacturing considering worker fatigue and skill

admitted_suites.rationale: Cloud manufacturing service composition with bi-objective time-cost trade-offs and worker-to-service matching. The alpha/beta worker pricing model is deterministically converted into candidate costs.

admitted_suites.name: QFBS (QACOForge Benchmarking Suite)

source.title: QACOBench: A Reusable Benchmark Suite for QoS-Aware Service Composition

admitted_suites.rationale: 5,200 instances generated directly through the HTTP API: 2,600 feasibility-guaranteed and 2,600 non-guaranteed instances. Each group uses the same 26 configurations at 100 seeds. Versioned requests and the generation manifest support reproduction; no second generation or semantic-pair audit is required.

excluded_or_classified_candidates.name: QWS Dataset (v1 and v2)

source.title: Investigating QoS of Real-World Web Services

excluded_or_classified_candidates.exclusion_rationale: QWS is an empirical catalogue of isolated Web service measurements (2,507 services across 9 QoS parameters: response time, availability, throughput, successability, reliability, compliance, best practices, latency, documentation). It lacks business process workflow topologies, task dependency DAGs, candidate-to-task bindings, and composition-level objective criteria. Admitting QWS directly into QACOBench would require inventing artificial workflow structures, which violates our semantic admission contract.

excluded_or_classified_candidates.name: WS-DREAM Dataset
excluded_or_classified_candidates.exclusion_rationale: WS-DREAM provides distributed client-side QoS observation matrices (User x Service x Time). It is specifically formulated for QoS prediction, matrix factorization, and collaborative filtering tasks, rather than combinatorial workflow service selection and placement. No fixed workflow DAGs or constraint sets are defined.

excluded_or_classified_candidates.name: Web Service Challenges (WSC 2008, 2009, 2010)

source.title: Web Service Challenge: Evaluation of Semantic Web Service Composition

excluded_or_classified_candidates.exclusion_rationale: WSC benchmarks address semantic discovery and automated workflow synthesis based on IOPE (Inputs, Outputs, Preconditions, Effects). In WSC, the graph topology is unknown and must be discovered by automated planners. QACOBench evaluates QACO (Quality-Aware Service Composition), which solves the orthogonal problem of discrete binding optimization over known, fixed workflow structures. Importing WSC into QACOBench would conflate automated semantic discovery with combinatorial QoS binding.

excluded_or_classified_candidates.name: WSBen Benchmark Toolkit

source.title: WSBen: A Web Services Discovery and Composition Benchmark

excluded_or_classified_candidates.exclusion_rationale: Synthetic ontology generator designed to produce semantic concept graphs for matchmaking and semantic chaining. Does not define QoS multi-criteria utility functions, SLA constraint assertions, or concrete service execution candidates.

excluded_or_classified_candidates.name: PPDRL Framework

source.title: Privacy-Preserving Deep Reinforcement Learning for QoS-Aware Service Composition

excluded_or_classified_candidates.exclusion_rationale: PPDRL is a neural reinforcement learning framework rather than an independent benchmark dataset. The experimental evaluation in the paper draws raw QoS values from QWS and generates random service graphs dynamically in RAM during training epochs without distributing persistent, reproducible instance packages.

excluded_or_classified_candidates.name: SFC Service Function Chaining (PeerJ cs-603)

source.title: Service function chain placement and routing in software defined networks

excluded_or_classified_candidates.exclusion_rationale: Formulates VNF (Virtual Network Function) routing and packet queue scheduling with context-free grammars and packet arrival distributions. Does not map to discrete multi-alternative web service selection with static QoS attributes.

excluded_or_classified_candidates.name: P-MDP (Probabilistic Markov Decision Process for Dynamic Web Services)

source.title: Dynamic Service Composition under Uncertainty using Markov Decision Processes

excluded_or_classified_candidates.exclusion_rationale: Focuses on runtime dynamic adaptation under stochastic failure transitions using Bellman value iteration. The decision variables represent dynamic policy actions rather than static or pre-scheduled workflow binding packages.
